kind: Physical Chicago bare-metal qualification; Kubernetes reconciliation implementation validated locally

checks.test: four isolated peers ready on two physical Chicago hosts
all origins replicate in both directions, including sibling feeds
33 MiB individual body replicates with exact bytes
canonical and private paths reject missing client certificates
cross-provider replication continues during a proven private failure
private failure has no canonical data fallback
private path recovers and replicas catch up
cold sibling restart restores the full corpus
previous staging image and topology image replicate in both directions
upgraded peer backfills all retained objects
namespace tombstones replicate to every node
all nodes finish ready and caught up without memory pressure

capture.filter: Cilium VXLAN on UDP 8472; inner source or destination matches the four fixture PodIPs
capture.broadCaptureLimitation: The earlier unscoped node-pair capture reported two unconsumed public-interface filter hits on one host; it is not used to claim zero public traffic for all node activity. The repeated fixture-filtered transfer had zero public captured and matched packets on both hosts.

continuity.limitation: Endpoint and pod snapshots, not continuous availability monitoring.

controller.publicationGate: Matching regional membership and current-boot route attestations on every eligible host
controller.validation: CAPI race tests and vet; Kura controller suite and vet; managed/default Helm render

limitations: No production reboot to validate persistence; host service is shared with the OVH implementation.
Bounded correctness and 200 Mbps transfers do not establish saturation throughput or N-1 capacity.
Santiago host transport and ORD–SCL private interconnect are not qualified.
Normal deployment must install the new controller before managed Chicago topology can publish; existing rollout/OnDelete holds remain effective.
